title: It is irrelevant to free choice whether its choice is impressed by a prior cause, so long as it follows practical judgement
source_text: X. Censent enim, ut loquuntur, impertinens esse libero arbitrio utrum suam electionem sibi impressam habeat a causa priori, an non: modo electio illa fiat ex judicio intellectus practici, qui diversas boni rationes circa opposita possit considerare, & voluntati proponere.
pass_a_gloss: X. For they judge, as they speak, that it is impertinent to free choice whether it has its election impressed on it by a prior cause, or not: provided that election be made from the judgement of the practical intellect, which can consider diverse reasons of good about opposites, and propose them to the will.
pass_b_english: In their phrase, it is 'irrelevant' to free choice whether its choosing is impressed on it by a prior cause or not.
What matters is that the choice comes from a judgement of the practical intellect, which is able to weigh different kinds of good on opposite sides and set them before the will.

lemmas.gloss: that it is impertinent to free choice
from the judgement of the practical intellect

choices.why: The faculty of free decision; 'free choice' is kept throughout, with 'freedom' for libertas.
